title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Huang Paddles Back Out and the Whole Beach Rides the Wave
conditions.summary: Stocks posted their best day since April 2025 after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, snapping the S&P 500's seven-day losing streak. The Nasdaq jumped 6.5 percent and fear gauge VIX dropped about 25 percent.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: The S&P 500 rose 4.7% to 7,237, its best day since April 2025, ending a seven-session losing streak that had pushed it into a correction.
The Nasdaq Composite surged 6.5% to 24,090 and the Dow gained 3.0% (about 1,448 points) to 49,595; the Russell 2000 added about 3.4%.
The spark: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, effective immediately, after he stepped down on November 12; Nvidia closed up about 31%.
Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ opened nearly 8% higher, its biggest opening gain since 1999, and the market held most of the gain into the close.
Nine of 11 S&P sectors rose; technology led with a 9% gain and communication services rose 5%, while energy (-1.3%) and consumer staples (-0.1%) slipped.
Some strategists said part of the move was mechanical, driven by short covering and options-dealer hedging.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: The S&P Global flash manufacturing PMI came in at 54.5, matching forecasts; the services PMI slipped to 54.7 versus 55.6 expected. Markets barely reacted.
The 10-year Treasury yield settled near 4.93%, roughly 2 basis points lower, while the 2-year rose about 2 basis points to 4.67%.
The dollar index climbed about 0.5% to roughly 104.3, a 19-month high.
WTI crude fell about 3.9% to settle near $80.17 a barrel, a three-month low, as Libya's Sharara pipeline reopened.
Futures still price a strong chance of a Fed rate hike at the December 9 meeting; this week is the last stretch of Fed commentary before the blackout.
The VIX fell about 25% to 27.05 from 35.89 on Friday.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: NVDA (Nvidia): +31.5% — Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO, adding more than $1 trillion in market value.
CRWV (CoreWeave): +22.3% — AI infrastructure names rebounded alongside Nvidia.
DELL (Dell): +20.5% — AI server maker bounced ahead of its earnings report Tuesday.
MU (Micron): +19.0% — memory chip stocks surged in the semiconductor rebound.
ZS (Zscaler): +17.7% — CrowdStrike agreed to buy it in an all-stock deal worth about $44 billion.
TSLA (Tesla): +11.5% — joined the broad megacap tech rally.
CRWD (CrowdStrike): -8.9% — fell on the cost of the Zscaler deal despite beating estimates and raising its outlook.
CAPR (Capricor Therapeutics): down more than 70% — the FDA declined to approve its Duchenne cell therapy deramiocel.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: CrowdStrike reported fiscal third-quarter revenue up 28% to $1.58 billion and raised its full-year outlook, but the stock fell about 9% on the Zscaler deal.
Zscaler reported first-quarter revenue up 20% and withdrew its outlook because of the pending merger; shares rose about 18%.
After the close, Zoom posted a third-quarter beat on both earnings and revenue and lifted its full-year outlook.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Agilent, Jacobs, Symbotic and Semtech also reported after the bell; their after-hours moves were not yet confirmed at press time.

sections.title: Business News
items: Nvidia's board said it voted unanimously to bring back Huang after consulting senior US officials; independent directors will finish their investigation, and Huang faces a public hearing December 3.
CrowdStrike will buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9 billion, a 34% premium, targeting $1 billion in annual revenue synergies.
Texas Pacific Land agreed to buy EagleRock Land for about $3 billion in stock, and CD&R is in talks to acquire Ashland for about $3.4 billion in cash.
Enphase Energy said it will cut 12% of its workforce.
President Trump said he expects China to buy another 250 Boeing aircraft.

sections.title: On Deck
items: Tuesday data: home prices at 8:00 AM CT, then Conference Board consumer confidence (forecast 92.1) and the Richmond Fed manufacturing index at 9:00 AM CT.
Before the open: Analog Devices, Medtronic, Best Buy, Dollar Tree, Dick's Sporting Goods, Burlington and J.M. Smucker.
After the close: Dell, Workday, Autodesk, HP and Nutanix.
Wednesday at 7:30 AM CT brings the PCE inflation report, the second estimate of third-quarter GDP, durable goods and jobless claims; markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Monday, November twenty third, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sinking into the water, the sky is pink and gold, and after a week of wipeouts, today was one gnarly comeback. Gus the wonder dog spent all afternoon chasing the swell up and down the sand, and he is one happy pup tonight. Give the Trade Wind surfers a good evening howl, Gus! Here's the final set. The S and P five hundred jumped four point seven percent to about seven thousand two hundred thirty seven. That's its best day since April of last year, and it snapped a seven day losing streak. The Nasdaq Composite surged six and a half percent to about twenty four thousand ninety. The Dow gained three percent, or about one thousand four hundred fifty points, to about forty nine thousand five hundred ninety five. Small caps in the Russell two thousand rose about three point four percent. The big swell came from Nvidia. Its board brought back Jensen Huang as chief executive, effective right away, after he stepped down on November twelfth. Nvidia rode that wave all the way to the beach, up about thirty one percent, adding more than a trillion dollars in value. Now that's a true Kahuna. Gus, that one's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! Technology stocks led, up about nine percent as a group. Nine of eleven sectors rose, while energy and consumer staples slipped. Some pros say part of this was short covering, so don't expect glassy water every day. Wind and weather now. The fear gauge, the V I X, dropped about twenty five percent to around twenty seven. The ten year Treasury yield settled near four point nine three percent, down about two basis points. The dollar rose about half a percent to a nineteen month high. Crude oil fell almost four percent to around eighty dollars a barrel, and gold rose about three percent. Bitcoin barely moved. A survey of service businesses came in a bit softer than expected, but nobody cared today. Traders still see a good chance the Fed raises rates on December ninth. In the lineup, CoreWeave climbed twenty two percent, Dell twenty percent, and Micron nineteen percent. Zscaler rose about eighteen percent after CrowdStrike agreed to buy it in an all stock deal worth about forty four billion dollars. CrowdStrike beat estimates and raised its outlook, but it still wiped out, down about nine percent. Tesla hung ten, up about eleven and a half percent. And Capricor Therapeutics sank more than seventy percent after the F D A declined to approve its Duchenne therapy. On the tide chart tonight, Zoom posted a beat on earnings and revenue and raised its outlook. Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Agilent, Jacobs and Symbotic also reported after the bell. Beach talk: Texas Pacific Land is buying EagleRock Land for about three billion dollars, Enphase is cutting twelve percent of its workforce, and the President said he expects China to buy two hundred fifty more Boeing jets. Tomorrow's forecast. Consumer confidence and the Richmond Fed survey land at nine A M Central. Before the bell, Analog Devices, Medtronic, Best Buy and Dollar Tree report. After the close, Dell, Workday, Autodesk and H P. Then Wednesday at seven thirty A M Central brings the big P C E inflation report before Thanksgiving. So wax that board and catch the Dawn Patrol tomorrow morning. And hey, want me to call a wave for you? Look up any stock, E T F or futures contract in the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will tell you how it's breaking. This is information, not advice.
